Advanced Setup

Source: vignettes/AdvancedSetup.Rmd
AdvancedSetup.Rmd

Progressive Elaboration

Advanced setup for SimBA is how SimBA implements progressive elaboration: complex models are derived from simpler ones through elaboration. Each advanced setup function modifies a single feature. These setup functions have the form:

setup_feature(name, xds_obj, options, ix)

where

  • name is the setup method;
  • xds_obj is an xds model object;
  • options are setup options, a named list;
  • ix is the species index.

The setup function modifies xds_obj and returns the modified object.

Each section this gives an list of advanced setup options by area, a brief description, and links to other documentation. In these lists, some of the setup options are listed in more than one location.

The XY jInterface

Information about parasite transmission between mosquitoes (X) and humans (Y) through blood feeding has three parts: blood feeding, exposure, and transmission. Transmission is an emergent feature of blood feeding, but malaria importation through visitors is also handled

Blood Feeding

In SimBA, blood feeding is understood as the result of mosquitoes searching for blood hosts. Each blood host has a search weight, which is used to compute availability.

  • blood_search_weights — set up or change the search weights for the human (or host) population strata
  • other_blood_hosts – set up the of other blood hosts as a variable.
  • blood_traps – set up the of traps that capture blood feeding mosquitoes as a variable
  • setup_F_circadian – set up a circadian function, the mosquito part of a function translates spent into at risk.
  • setup_f – by default, blood feeding rates (\(f\)) are not computed as a functional response to available blood hosts, but it is an advanced setup option.
  • setup_q – by default, the human fractions (\(q\)) are not computed as a functional response to availabile blood hosts, but it is an advanced setup option.

Exposure

Exposure is a core concept in malaria epidemiology, and it is a part of the blood feeding and transmission interface.

  • Local Exposure

    • setup_timespent – set up or modify the time spent matrix.
    • setup_blood_search_weights – set up or modify the blood search weights for each population stratum.
    • split_base_by_search_weights – a utility to stratify the model by biting

  • Travel Malaria

    • setup_time_away – the parameter describes time spent by each population stratum outside the spatial domain defined by the patches
    • setup_travel_eir – the average daily EIR experienced by each population stratum while traveling
    • split_base_by_travel – a stratification utility. It segments the population and modifies the blood search weights.

  • Environmental Heterogeneity: setup_exposure — this changes the model about the distribution of the expectation for infectious biting.

  • Pre-erythrocytic immunity is defined by the XH modules. Parameters can be changed using change_XH_pars

Visitors

Information about visitors is used by the transmission module.

  • setup_visitors — modify the variable to describing the of human visitors, who get are bitten by mosquitoes. During setup, the variable is set to zero.
  • setup_vis_kappa — modify the interface variable that describes the of visitors. During setup, it is set to zero.

The ML Interface

The ML interface manages the habitats, egg laying and emergence. At basic setup, the habitat membership vector is used to construct the habitat matrix that \(N\) sums adults emerging from aquatic habitats by patch.

To build models,

  • add_habitat_buffer

Habitats and Egg Laying

  • setup_habitat_search_weights – set up or modify the habitat search weights.
  • setup_bad_habitats – modify the availability of habitats, water where mosquitoes would lay eggs but that would never support development of adults. During setup, the variable is set to zero.
  • setup_ovitraps – modify the availability of habitats, water where mosquitoes would lay eggs but that would never support development of adults. During setup, the variable is set to zero.
  • setup_nu – by default, egg laying rates (\(\nu\)) are not computed as a functional response to available, but it is an advanced setup option.

Adult Mosquitoes

Bionomics

Some of the parameters describing mosquito behavior or ecology are set up to be computed as a baseline that is modified by control. This is slightly misleading, because some models can compute the effects and effect sizes of control as a functional response to contact with some kind of vector control. By default, these parameters are set to constant values and checked, but they can be modified using advanced setup options:

  • setup_f – set up or modify blood feeding rates or the way they are computed
  • setup_q – set up or modify the human fractions or the way they are computed
  • setup_nu – set up or modify egg laying rates or the way they are computed
  • setup_g – set up or modify mosquito mortality rates or the way they are computed
  • setup_sigma – set up or modify patch emigration rates or the way they are computed
  • setup_mu – set up or modify emigration loss fractions or the way they are computed
  • setup_K_matrix – set up or modify the mosquito dispersal matrix or the way it is computed
  • setup_eip – set up or modify the EIP or the way they are computed

For more information, see Supplement 7.

Malaria Importation

  • Travel Malaria (also see Exposure, above)

    • setup_time_away – the parameter describes time spent by each population stratum outside the spatial domain defined by the patches
    • setup_travel_eir – the average daily EIR experienced by each population stratum while traveling
    • split_base_by_travel – a stratification utility to segment populations to model heterogeneous travel.

  • Visitors

    • setup_visitors — modify the variable to describing the of human visitors, who get are bitten by mosquitoes. During setup, the variable is set to zero.
    • setup_vis_kappa — modify the interface variable that describes the of visitors. During setup, it is set to zero.

Immature Mosquito Ecology

  • setup_capacity

Malaria Epidemiology

Demography

  • setup_births – set up or modify the birth rates for the human or host population
  • setup_deaths – set up or modify the death rates for the human or host population
  • setup_migration – set up migration: individuals move among strata
  • stratify_by_age – set up an age-structured model, a stratifiction utility

Mass Treatment

  • setup_mda – set up mass drug administration
  • setup_msat – set up mass screen and treat

Progressive Stratification

  • setup_stratify_by_age – set up an age-structured model with aging and age-specific mortality
  • split_base_by_travel – segment the existing strata for heterogeneous travel malaria
  • split_base_by_care_seeking – segment the existing strata for heterogeneous care seeking
  • split_base_by_search_weights – segment existing strata for heterogeneous biting

Exogenous Forcing

In SimBA, exogenous forcing can be implemented in several ways.

  • Any dynamical term can be used to force the system by configuring a trivial module.
  • The mosquito bionomic parameters can be set up to be computed as a function of resource availability or weather variables (see above)
  • Vector control

Trivial Modules

Trivial modules set up forced_by, so

  • change_mean_forcing – changes the value of the mean forcing function

  • The Seasonal Pattern Function, \(S(t)\)

    • change_F_season – replaces the seasonal pattern function with a new function
    • change_season – replace _par and rebuild the seasonal pattern function

  • The Trend Pattern Function, \(T(t)\)

    • change_F_trend – replaces the trend pattern function with a new function
    • change_trend – replace _par and rebuild the trend pattern function

  • The Shock Function, \(K(t)\)

    • change_F_shock – replaces the shock function with a new function
    • change_shock – replace _par and rebuild the pattern function

  • Relative Biting by Age

    • change_F_age – replaces the function to compute relative biting rates by age with a new function
    • change_age – replace _par and rebuild the function that computes relative biting rates by age

  • rebuild_forcing_functions

Weather Variables

Several variables

  • setup_rainfall – add an exogenous variable describing rainfall

  • setup_temperature – add an exogenous variable describing temperature

  • setup_humidity – add an exogenous variable describing humidity

Resources

  • setup_blood_search_weights – modify the blood search weights
  • setup_other_blood_hosts – modify the availability of alternative blood hosts
  • setup_blood_traps – modify the availability of traps that capture blood feeding mosquitoes
  • setup_habitat_search_weights – modify the habitat search weights
  • setup_bad_habitats – modify the availability of bad habitats, water where mosquitoes would lay eggs but that would never support development of adults. During setup, the variable is set to zero.
  • setup_ovitraps – modify the availability of ovitraps
  • setup_sugar – set up a variable for the availability of sugar

Internals

Ports and Junctions

To enable progressive elaboration, xds model object must include structures to handle the advanced options.

Most of these features will not be used most of the time, but they must be designed in and present for the software to work at all.

Extensibility for variables involved in one of the interfaces or part of a dynamical component are handled through ports and junctions: objects designed to handle heterogeneity and exogenous forcing.

A port is an object that makes any parameter or term extensible: most ports are set up by default to have no effect, but it can be modified to have an effect through advanced setup.

A junction activates a set of ports.

Junctions handle weather variables, intervention coverage, resource dynamics, baseline mosquito bionomics, vector control effect sizes, mass pharmaceutical interventions, and malaria importation. Advanced setup options to configure ports are discussed in the following sections.
